findings.title: Reject conflicting release and workbook provenance before issuing source proof
findings.description: roundtrip validates self-carried raw-cell and schema digests but never checks source.release, workbookSha256, URL, worksheet or member digest against the pinned workbook. proof then unconditionally emits global RELEASE and SHA256. Independent actual-source mutations of each of these five fields still pass proof. In particular a record labelled unreviewed-other-release or carrying workbookSha256=all-zero returns a proof claiming the original 2023-corrected-20260327-main release and original workbook. This can misattribute source-labelled staging after JSON record handling; it does not establish a production leak or admitted dataset.
findings.recommendation: Bind source release/workbook/URL constants and worksheet/member/digest against a trusted index derived from the exact retained workbook before returning roundtrip/proof; preserve original row/cell/schema checks. Require conflicting provenance to fail rather than relabel evidence with hard-coded proof fields.
findings.acceptance: The five retained mutation probes must reject; the 192 actual records and existing 7 tests must still pass.
